keep_kunder4.zh_canonical: 聽另一方之詞 ※比較 parte inaudita
keep_kunder4.rationale: Canonical natural-justice maxim (the right to be heard); foundational doctrine in HK administrative law and judicial review jurisprudence. Absence of HK Cap. attestation reflects the Latin maxim's case-law primacy rather than doctrinal marginality.

Canonical doctrine of judicial review: an act exceeding the conferring statute's authority is void. Central to HK common-law administrative law (k_zh=5 attests Chinese rendering; English k_en=0 reflects case-law primacy of the Latin form).

keep_kunder4.zh_canonical: 韋恩斯伯里原則〔關於酌情權行使的合理性測試原則〕
keep_kunder4.rationale: Wednesbury unreasonableness — foundational ground of judicial review in HK common-law tradition (Associated Provincial Picture Houses v Wednesbury Corp.). Doctrinal centrality is independent of statute-text frequency: it is a case-law standard.

Prerogative writ of certiorari — quashing remedy in HK judicial review. k_en=8 attestation but k_zh=0: the Latin form predominates in English texts while Chinese statutory texts use functional rendering (移審撤銷令); doctrinal centrality justifies retention.

Prerogative writ of mandamus — compulsion remedy in HK judicial review. k_en=8 strong English attestation; k_zh=2 reflects Latin-form dominance over Chinese functional rendering. Pair with certiorari completes the core JR remedy set.

drop.rationale: Civil Service Regulations: k=0/0 in HK Cap. e-Legislation (regulations themselves are subsidiary instruments not lemmatised in the corpus index). Doctrinal substance covered by 'civil service' and 'public officer' (kept).

drop.zh_canonical: 任何人不得成為自己案件的法官
drop.rationale: Nemo judex in causa sua: k=0/0; the rule against bias is doctrinally entailed by 'audi alteram partem' (kept) under the umbrella of natural justice. Drop the duplicative Latin maxim to economise.

Eminent domain: k=0/0; this is a US/civil-law term of art for compulsory acquisition. The HK common-law equivalent is 'resumption' under the Lands Resumption Ordinance (Cap. 124), not 'eminent domain'. Drop as non-HK.

Administrative Secretary: k=0/0; the HK office is the 'Chief Secretary for Administration' (政務司司長). Surface form 'Administrative Secretary' is unattested. Drop; institutional substance covered by 'civil service' and 'Public Service Commission'.
Customs duty: k_en=2; specific tax type subsumed by the 'Customs and Excise' institution (kept) and the broader 'tax' lemma. Drop for sub-area economy.

Orders in Council: k_en=0; colonial-era Imperial regulatory instrument largely supplanted post-1997 by HK Ordinances and subsidiary legislation. Drop as historically residual; HK regulatory acts represented by Ordinance, regulation, bylaw, Gazette.
Quasi-judicial: k_en=3, k_zh=0; descriptive adjective whose substance is captured by 'Administrative Appeals Board' (kept) and 'judicial review' (kept). Drop.

Taxation: morphological derivative of lemma 'tax' (3380, kept). Drop per consolidation rule. The administrative-law concept of fiscal power is preserved by 'tax', 'revenue', 'salaries tax', 'Tax Reserve Certificate'.
Value-added tax (VAT): k_en=0; HK does not levy VAT. The Chinese rendering 增值稅 attests in cross-border/PRC contexts only. Drop as non-HK.
Withholding tax: k_en=3, k_zh=0; specific tax mechanism, sub-area economy favours dropping for higher-frequency fiscal terms.
Deregistration: morphological derivative of 'registration' (2973, kept) — the negative inflection of the same administrative procedure. Drop per consolidation rule.

Passport: k=8/8 attestation but the term is a concrete travel document rather than a doctrinal administrative-law concept. Drop to respect the administrative_procedure cap (≤10) in favour of higher-doctrine candidates.
Ratepayer: k=1/1; municipal-rates concept rare in HK Cap. text. Drop.

promote.rationale: 'Public servant' (公務人員) is the HK Cap. canonical category for personnel exercising public power and a key referent in the Prevention of Bribery Ordinance (Cap. 201). High knn similarity (0.840) with 'public officer' (kept) confirms semantic adjacency without redundancy: PoBO uses 'public servant' as the broader umbrella.

Marine Department (海事處) is a HK statutory department under Cap. 369 family of shipping ordinances. Strong attestation (8/8) and knn alignment with administrative-departmental cluster. Adds departmental-bureaucracy coverage to balance the institutions sub-area.

Justice of the Peace (太平紳士) is a HK-specific honorary statutory office under the Justices of the Peace Ordinance (Cap. 510), exercising visiting powers over places of detention. Strong attestation (8/8). Note: prefer this fuller form over duplicate 6232 ('justice of the peace' lower-case).

District Officer (民政事務專員) is a HK-specific institution heading District Offices under the Home and Youth Affairs Bureau, exercising statutory functions in the District Administration Scheme. Adequate attestation (7/6) and high cluster alignment.

Government Chemist (政府化驗師) is a HK statutory office whose certificates have evidentiary status under multiple ordinances (Dangerous Drugs Ordinance Cap. 134, etc.). Strong attestation (8/8). HK-specific institutional fixture.

'By notice' (藉憲報公告) is the canonical HK Cap. formula for triggering subsidiary legislative effect via Gazette publication; knn confidence 1.00 marks it as the modal regulatory-act phrase. Pairs with 'Gazette' (kept) to operationalise notice-based law-making.

Code of conduct (行為守則) — quasi-regulatory instrument widely used in HK Cap. (Cap. 622 Companies Ordinance, Cap. 571 Securities and Futures Ordinance). Strong attestation; complements formal regulation/bylaw with soft-law instruments.

Code of practice (工作守則) — distinct quasi-regulatory instrument frequent in HK Cap. (Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance Cap. 486, Occupational Safety regimes). Strong attestation; complements 'code of conduct' as the operational soft-law sibling.

'Regulatory' (規管的) — the modifier defining regulatory power as a public-law category (regulatory authority, regulatory regime). knn similarity 0.921 (very high). Doctrinally indispensable adjective for the regulatory-state dimension of HK public administration.
'Authorize' (授權) — operative verb of delegated authority. Foundational to delegated-legislation analysis, ultra vires review, and conferral of statutory power. Strong attestation (8/8).

'Public interest' (公眾利益) — touchstone criterion for the lawful exercise of administrative discretion in HK common-law judicial review (Wednesbury, proportionality). Strong attestation (8/8); doctrinally central.

'Taxpayer' (納稅人) — subject of the fiscal-administrative relation; canonical noun in Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112). High knn similarity (0.770) with the kept fiscal cluster (tax, salaries tax, revenue). Distinct lemma from 'tax', not a derivative.
'Taxable' (應課稅) — qualifying adjective central to the structure of HK fiscal law (Cap. 112), distinguishing the assessable base. Strong attestation (8/8); knn similarity 0.794 to fiscal cluster.

confidence_self_assessment.rationale: High confidence on the core institutional retentions (HKSAR organs, HK statutory commissions, regulatory-act lexicon) and on the five Latin/common-law doctrinal exceptions (audi alteram partem, ultra vires, Wednesbury, certiorari, mandamus), which are jointly canonical for HK administrative law. Lower confidence on a small number of sub-area assignments at the boundary of governance_institutions vs hk_specific_institutions (e.g., Marine Department, Justice of the Peace), and on the consolidation choice between 'tax' and 'taxation' (kept 'tax' as lemma; either is defensible). The administrative_procedure cap forced the drop of 'passport' (8/8 attested but doctrinally peripheral) and 'deregistration' (morphological inverse of registration), both judgement calls.

weakest_decisions.concern: Dropping 'passport' (8/8) was forced by sub-area cap rather than doctrinal weakness; arguably an HK-specific identity instrument worth keeping if cap relaxed.
Dropping 'taxation' as morphological derivative of 'tax': the abstract administrative concept of taxation as a public-power function is arguably distinct from the bare noun 'tax'; rule-driven choice.

Dropping 'deregistration' as morphological derivative of 'registration': the inverse procedure is administratively distinct (different statutory triggers, different consequences) but ruled out per consolidation.
'Orders in Council' (k_en=0, k_zh=8): asymmetric attestation; dropped as historically residual but the Chinese rendering's strength might support a kunder4 retention if the slot were available.
Promoting 'public interest' to public_power_doctrines is correct doctrinally but the term is also generic across legal domains; classification is defensible but borderline.

notes: Curation prioritises HK Cap.-attested administrative-law lexicon while reserving the five exception slots for the Latin / case-law doctrinal apparatus of natural justice and prerogative writs (audi alteram partem, ultra vires, Wednesbury, certiorari, mandamus), whose absence from statute-text frequency reflects their case-law primacy in HK common-law tradition rather than doctrinal marginality. Sub-area redistribution: administrative_procedure trimmed to 10 (cap) by dropping 'passport' and 'deregistration'; public_power_doctrines built up from 2 (administrative, judicial review) to 10 via the kunder4 doctrines and three promotions (regulatory, authorize, public interest); regulatory_acts brought to 10 via 'by notice', 'code of conduct', 'code of practice'. Fiscal terms classified as 'other' (no sub-area listed for fiscal/revenue lexicon, but doctrinally central to HK public administration via Inland Revenue Ordinance Cap. 112). One latent duplicate noted in input: term 6232 'justice of the peace' (lower-case) duplicates 2130 'Justice of the Peace; J.P.' — promoted only the canonical capitalised form.
